question: Milan city centre was hit by a wave of violent clashes and looting on 17 and 18 October 2026. Press reports indicate that protesters had been encouraged to gather by an Instagram account that had been created on 4 October, that TikTok was then used to boost this initiative’s visibility, and that better-organised groups coordinated their efforts on Telegram.
More than 160 people were apprehended, around 80 % of whom were minors. Confcommercio estimates that these incidents caused damage estimated at more than EUR 500 000.

While Article 28 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 on a single market for digital services requires providers of online platforms that are accessible to minors to safeguard and protect this demographic, Articles 34-5 thereof compel providers of very large online platforms to assess and mitigate systemic public security risks. In view of the above, could the Commission answer the following: 1.

Will it, pursuant to Article 67 of the Digital Services Act, ask Meta and TikTok to provide information concerning the account that organised this gathering, the content that was used to boost its reach, the time it took these platforms to remove the posts in question and any coordinated efforts undertaken by organised groups to further disseminate this gathering?
Will it clarify whether Telegram is subject to the enhanced DSA obligations and verify the user data that this platform has made available?

Will it assess whether the measures taken by platforms under Articles 28 and 35 are fit for the purposes of preventing minors from organising violent urban gatherings and making these initiatives go viral?
